title: Keyboard Manager shortcuts cannot override Windows shortcuts
next_action: Approve the diagnostic design and request the focused Win+Arrow comparison matrix.

judgment.rationale: The Win+Arrow reproduction is clear, but the failure could be hook matching, shell suppression timing, or replacement-input injection. Existing fork investigation should continue rather than competing work being opened.
evidence: Win+Left and Win+Right invoke Windows Snap instead of Home and End.
No diagnostic archive or hook/injection trace is attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve or resume the existing fork investigation; request only the evidence needed to select the failing input boundary.

fix_assessment.rationale: The fork issue is an active investigation, not a confirmed implementation. No competing fix plan is proposed.

proposed_fixes.title: Instrument Win+Arrow matching, suppression, and injection
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Provisional: the low-level hook may miss the shell-reserved event, suppress too late, or fail to inject the replacement key.
plan: Capture hook initialization, settings load, shortcut match, modifier restoration, SendInput result, and suppression return.
Compare normal/elevated PowerToys, Snap enabled/disabled, and Win+Arrow versus Win+A.
Select a behavioral fix only after the trace identifies the failing boundary.
verification: Confirm the trace identifies matching, suppression, or injection as the failing step.
Verify Win+Left and Win+Right produce Home and End without Snap.

confidence.rationale: The reproduction is strong, but several code paths remain plausible and no trace is available.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager maps Win+Arrow to Home/End, but Windows Snap wins; the current evidence does not identify why the remap path fails.
known_information: Win+Left maps to Home and Win+Right maps to End.
Stable and preview builds are affected.
The reporter supplied no diagnostic archive.
An existing fork investigation is public at https://github.com/MuyuanMS/PowerToys/issues/638.
inferences: The problem may be specific to shell-reserved Win+Arrow handling.
A timing or deferred-injection change is possible but unproven.
issue_context.analysis: Because Keyboard Manager already has matching, suppression, and injection logic, changing one layer blindly could regress other mappings. A small diagnostic matrix is the lowest-risk next step.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full discussion and linked historical issues.
Focused code areas are KeyboardManager::HookProc, KeyboardManager::HandleKeyboardHookEvent, HandleShortcutRemapEvent, and OS-level remapping tests.
No confirmed upstream fix exists; the public fork investigation is the existing work item.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic captured immediately after reproducing Win+Arrow.
information_gaps.why_needed: It may show hook initialization, settings, and injection failures.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once, then add `/bugreport` immediately afterward.

information_gaps.information: Results for normal/elevated PowerToys, Snap enabled/disabled, and Win+Arrow versus Win+A.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates shell reservation, integrity-level, and general remapping failures.

design.root_cause: Not established; hook matching, shell suppression timing, and replacement injection remain competing explanations.
evidence: The shell action occurs instead of the mapped key.
Keyboard Manager has a low-level hook, suppression path, and virtual input injection.
No trace identifies which stage fails.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The handler matches shortcuts, restores modifiers, injects replacement input, and returns suppression.
implementation_steps.change: Add temporary or test-gated diagnostics for match state, modifier state, SendInput result, and suppression return before selecting a behavioral change.
implementation_steps.code_block: log(match, vkCode, modifiers); sent = SendVirtualInput(inputs); log(sent); return matched ? 1 : 0;
edge_cases: Do not ship verbose diagnostics or log sensitive text.
Preserve repeat, AltGr, modifier restoration, and elevation behavior.
tests: Extend Win+Left/Right and Win+A coverage after the failing branch is known.

verify: Run the requested normal/elevated and Snap on/off comparison matrix.
Verify Home/End insertion and absence of Snap in an interactive desktop.
risks: A guessed suppression change could break modifier and repeat behavior.
Deferred injection could affect shortcut timing.
alternatives: Declare Win+Arrow unsupported; rejected because the current product behavior implies remapping support.
Change SendInput timing blindly; rejected without a trace.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. To resolve the recorded uncertainty, please provide:

1. A fresh diagnostic captured immediately after reproducing Win+Arrow. Collection: Reproduce once, then add `/bugreport` immediately afterward.
2. Results for normal/elevated PowerToys, Snap enabled/disabled, and Win+Arrow versus Win+A. Collection: Report the four comparison results in a numbered issue comment.
